questions.question_text: Which classification correctly describes the parity of $f(x) = 2x^{3} - 5x$?

options.why: Confused rotational origin symmetry with line symmetry across the $y$-axis.
Failed to factor out the common negative sign from $-2x^{3} + 5x$.

questions.question_text: Which of the following functions is an even function?

options.why: This function contains only odd powers of $x$ and is odd because $f(-x) = -f(x)$, not even.
The linear term $-3x$ mixes an odd power with even powers, so $f(-x) \neq f(x)$.
The non-zero constant term $+4$ prevents this predominantly odd-degree polynomial from being even or odd.

questions.solution_text:
For $f(x) = 3x^{4} - 8x^{2} + 5$:
$f(-x) = 3(-x)^{4} - 8(-x)^{2} + 5$
$= 3x^{4} - 8x^{2} + 5$
$= f(x)$
Since $f(-x) = f(x)$, $f(x) = 3x^{4} - 8x^{2} + 5$ is an even function.
By contrast, for $f(x) = 4x^{3} - 9x$, $f(-x) = -4x^{3} + 9x = -f(x)$, which is odd rather than even.

questions.question_text: Which classification correctly describes the parity of $f(x) = x^{3} + 3x^{2} - 2$?

options.text: Even, because the highest power that survives the test is $3x^{2}$
options.why: Tested only the quadratic term; the terms $x^{3}$ and $-2$ must also satisfy $f(-x) = f(x)$, and $x^{3}$ does not.

options.text: Odd, because the leading term $x^{3}$ is an odd power
options.why: A single odd-power term does not make the whole function odd; the remaining terms $3x^{2} - 2$ are unchanged by $x \to -x$, so $f(-x) \neq -f(x)$.

options.text: Both even and odd, because it contains both odd and even powers
options.why: Only the zero function is both even and odd; a mixture of odd and even powers gives neither.

questions.solution_text:
$f(-x) = (-x)^{3} + 3(-x)^{2} - 2$
$= -x^{3} + 3x^{2} - 2$
Compare with $f(x) = x^{3} + 3x^{2} - 2$: the $x^{3}$ term has changed sign but $3x^{2} - 2$ has not, so $f(-x) \neq f(x)$.
Compare with $-f(x) = -x^{3} - 3x^{2} + 2$: the $3x^{2}$ and $-2$ terms do not match, so $f(-x) \neq -f(x)$.
The function is therefore neither even nor odd.

questions.question_text: What is the parity of the rational function $f(x) = \dfrac{3x}{x^{2} + 9}$?

options.why: Assumed the even denominator $x^{2}+9$ makes the entire quotient even.
Failed to recognize that an odd numerator divided by an even denominator is odd.

questions.question_text: If $f(x)$ is an odd function such that $f(5) = 9$, what is the value of $f(-5)$?

options.why: Applied the even-function rule $f(-x) = f(x)$ instead of the odd-function rule.
Negated the input instead of the output, reporting $-5$ rather than $-f(5)$.

options.text: It cannot be determined without the rule for $f(x)$
options.why: The parity property fixes $f(-5) = -f(5)$ for every odd function, so the explicit rule is not needed.

questions.solution_text:
By definition, an odd function satisfies $f(-x) = -f(x)$ for all $x$ in its domain.
Substituting $x = 5$ gives:
$f(-5) = -f(5)$
$= -(9)$
$= -9$

questions.question_text: What is the parity of $f(x) = x\sqrt{4 - x^{2}}$ on its natural domain $[-2, 2]$?

options.why: Observed the even radical $\sqrt{4-x^{2}}$ and ignored the factor of $x$.
Assumed that radical expressions cannot possess odd symmetry.

questions.question_text: What is the parity of the exponential function $f(x) = 5^{x} - 5^{-x}$?

options.why: Confused $5^{x} - 5^{-x}$ with the even sum $5^{x} + 5^{-x}$.
Assumed all exponential expressions are inherently neither even nor odd.

questions.question_text: If $f(x)$ is an odd function and $g(x)$ is an even function, what is the parity of their product $h(x) = f(x)g(x)$?

options.why: Assumed the even function dominates the product.
Assumed multiplying functions of different parity always produces neither.

questions.solution_text:
$h(-x) = f(-x)g(-x)$
$= (-f(x))(g(x))$
$= -f(x)g(x)$
$= -h(x)$
Since $h(-x) = -h(x)$, the product is odd.

questions.question_text:
Let $f(x)$ be any function defined on all real numbers.
Which of the following expressions is guaranteed to be an even function?

options.why: If $f(x) = 0$, $f(x)+x = x$ which is odd rather than even.
This expression is always odd because $(-f(-x) - (-f(x))) = -(f(x)-f(-x))$.
If $f(x)$ is odd, $[f(x)]^{3}$ is also odd rather than even.

questions.solution_text:
Let $h(x) = f(x^{2})$.
$h(-x) = f((-x)^{2})$
$= f(x^{2})$
$= h(x)$
Since $h(-x) = h(x)$ regardless of the formula for $f$, $f(x^{2})$ is always even.
